title: Lobster Roll
subtitle: New England lobster in buttered brioche roll
excerpt: The ultimate New England sandwich: cold cooked lobster meat dressed in a little good mayonnaise and celery, served in a toasted, buttered brioche hot dog bun. The best possible thing to eat on a warm day near the sea.

recipe.sourceNotes: The lobster roll is the signature sandwich of the New England coastline, particularly associated with Maine and Connecticut. Two distinct styles exist: the Maine-style cold lobster roll (lobster meat dressed with mayonnaise and served cold) and the Connecticut-style hot lobster roll (lobster meat warmed in melted butter and served hot in a buttered roll). The Maine version is the more widely known internationally. The defining feature of the authentic lobster roll is the bread: a top-split hot dog bun, toasted in butter on both flat sides. The lobster filling should be lightly dressed; the quality of the lobster is the point and should not be overwhelmed by heavy seasoning.

content.text: Use the best-quality cooked lobster available; freshly cooked is ideal. The dressing should be restrained; enough mayonnaise to bind and moisten, not enough to mask the flavour of the lobster. The roll must be toasted in butter; an untoasted roll is not a lobster roll.

items.preparation: cooked; meat extracted from claws and tail; roughly chopped
use brioche hot dog buns if available; split and toasted flat-side down in butter

content.text: Mix the lobster meat with the mayonnaise, diced celery, lemon juice, and chives. Season with salt and white pepper. The mixture should be lightly coated, not saturated. Refrigerate until ready to serve.
Butter the flat cut sides of the buns generously. Toast in a dry pan over medium-high heat until golden and crisp, about 1 to 2 minutes per side.
Fill the toasted rolls generously with the lobster mixture. Serve immediately with a pile of crisps or fries.
